messages:
iris: Heads up — p95 gen latency SLOs tripped in eu-west-1 starting ~11:02 UTC. Alert spam from alerts-bot.
jay: I'm seeing continuous batching pressure on a small subset of pods. queue depth climbs and wait_for_fill sits at 200-300ms. max_batch_size=64 on those models.
marta: Short sequences + high burstiness = long waits for batch fill. Can we try lowering max_batch_size temporarily? 64 seems aggressive for this workload.
sean: Autoscaler didn't react because CPU stayed low. We're blocked on request queueing, not compute. Scaling on CPU isn't enough.
laura: Also noticed admission controller token bucket is exhausted because of an imbalance between regional routing and capacity. We get head-of-line blocking and then admission starts dropping. Feedback loop. :sob:
iris: Repro notes: bursty client pattern -> initial packets land, runtime waits to pack up to 64 -> more arrivals don't fit due to per-pod inflight limits -> latency balloons, client retries -> more bursts.
jay: Tentative mitigations: 1) reduce max_batch_size to 32 2) enable partial_flush / max_wait_ms=80 3) change autoscaler to use queue_wait_seconds p95.
laura: Adding to that: admission should expose token backlog and a soft reject path so requests can be routed to lower-capacity fallback models instead of queueing forever.
marta: Quick patch I can push: reduce wait_for_fill from 200ms -> 80ms and lower max_batch_size to 32 for eu-west-1 routing group. Rollback plan: revert in 10m if errors spike.
ops-bot: @oncall eu-west notified. Canary policy: apply to 10% of pods first.
sean: Also opened infra ticket to add a scaling metric: redwood_runtime_queue_wait_seconds_bucket. We should alarm when p95 > 100ms.
jay: Config snippet to try (apply to route eu-west-gpu):
```
admission:
  max_batch_size: 32
  wait_for_fill_ms: 80
  max_inflight_per_pod: 256
  soft_reject_threshold: 0.85
```
laura: Can we also temporarily enable the fallback model policy for the most latency-sensitive routes? Redirect 20% of excess requests to a lower-capacity-but-faster variant.
iris: I'm applying Marta's config to the 10% canary now. Will watch p95 / retries / error-rate.
devops-bot: deploy started -> canary 10% (10 pods). Expected rollout 2m.
marta: If this reduces head-of-line waits, it proves batching fill waits were the root cause. If not, we look deeper at KV cache eviction and packing heuristics.
sean: For long term: switch autoscaler to use queue_wait_seconds and add admission controller metrics to the console. Also consider adaptive max_batch that reacts to current latency targets.
jay: Agreed. Short-term: apply patch, monitor for 10m, then either expand rollout or revert.
iris: Update: +6m after canary -> p95 down from 420ms -> 160ms, error-rate unchanged, retries down. Looks promising. :thumbsup:
laura: Nice. Let's keep canary for 30m then roll to 100% if stable. Open action items for autoscaler metric and fallback routing.
iris: Filing follow-ups: INFRA-3421 (autoscale metric), INFRA-3422 (admission soft-reject), RUN-981 (adaptive batching research).
ops-bot: @channel: SLO alert acknowledged and triaged.
